evidence.title: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum
evidence.text: The Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum is an American sports stadium located in the Exposition Park neighborhood of Los Angeles, California.

evidence.title: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum
evidence.text: The stadium serves as the home to the University of Southern California (USC) Trojans football team, and as the temporary home of the Los Angeles Rams of the National Football League (NFL).

evidence.title: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum
evidence.text: The Coliseum was home to the Rams from 1946 to 1979, when they moved to Anaheim Stadium in Anaheim, California, and is serving as their home stadium again until the completion of Los Angeles Stadium at Hollywood Park in Inglewood, California.

evidence.title: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum
evidence.text: The facility has a permanent seating capacity of 93,607 for USC football games, making it the largest football stadium in the Pac-12 Conference.

evidence.title: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum
evidence.text: For Rams games, capacity is at 93,607, giving it the largest capacity in the NFL.

evidence.title: 2013 Trinidad and Tobago Pro Bowl
